summary.title: Always be quitting
summary.one_liner: Learn why making yourself replaceable (“always be quitting”) frees you to grow into higher roles, with ten concrete habits such as documenting knowledge, delegating, and training your replacement.
keywords: automating yourself out of your job
takeaways: Being indispensable keeps you stuck in one job; being replaceable frees you to change projects or move up.
Document knowledge, plans, and meeting notes so colleagues do not depend on you in real time.
Avoid becoming the single point of contact: bring others to meetings and use shared mailing lists.
Train and delegate to others, and identify and coach your own replacement.
Stay responsible for your projects while doing this; it also raises the whole team's level and builds staff-engineer skills.
summary.summary: The author argues that engineers should act as if they could leave at short notice, which means making themselves replaceable rather than indispensable. The post lists ten concrete practices: documenting knowledge, long-term plans and meeting notes, bringing others to meetings, training and delegating to people, giving them power to decide, avoiding being the sole point of contact, identifying a replacement, and continuing to learn. It stresses that this does not mean abdicating responsibility, and that it benefits the whole team and builds staff/principal-level skills.
